name: Curaçao
summary: Curaçao has no forced heirship, so a will can leave the estate to anyone, though children and a spouse have statutory lump-sum rights. Curaçao has its own trust (since 2012) and a private foundation (stichting particulier fonds). The Hague Trusts Convention has been in force for Curaçao since 1 February 2024.
family_claims: The Caribbean Book 4 replaced the legitieme portie with mandatory statutory rights (a child's lump sum for upbringing and unpaid work, arts. 4:35-36 in the Sint Maarten text, and spousal rights). Curaçao's own text was not read.
foreign_law_note: No source read states Curaçao's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. A 2023 article says a conflict-of-laws ordinance for trusts was still intended.
trust_note: The HCCH extensions page lists Curaçao (extension 27 November 2023, in force 1 February 2024). Curaçao has a trust created by notarial deed since 1 January 2012 (secondary source). The stichting particulier fonds is a private foundation that may distribute to the founder's family and cannot run a business.
open_questions: Date Curaçao's Book 4 entered into force was not confirmed; a 2021 Dutch parliamentary question says Curaçao has no legitieme portie.
Statute articles for the Curaçao trust were not read (source is a paywalled summary).
Conflict rule for succession of foreign nationals not sourced.
